name: Edge Growth Plan
tagline: Protect the hairline. Reduce tension. Build a consistent care routine.
image_alt: A woman with long dark curls presses her fingertips along her hairline and side part.
overview: Hairline protection and consistent scalp care
Conditioning fragile hair and reducing friction
People experiencing edge breakage, styling-related tension or friction concerns
Styling tension, scalp comfort, hairline appearance, breakage observations and photo consistency
goal: Create a repeatable hairline-care routine that reduces avoidable mechanical stress, maintains scalp hygiene, conditions fragile hair around the edges and documents changes over time.
goal_note: Protecting the hairline comes before trying to stimulate it. A serum cannot compensate for a hairstyle that repeatedly pulls on the follicles.
pillars: Stop or substantially modify hairstyles that pull on the hairline. Avoid tight braids, tight ponytails, heavy extensions, repeated slicking and aggressive edge brushing.
Follow a scheduled scalp-cleansing interval that suits your scalp and styling routine. Keep the scalp clean without rough scrubbing.
Include a selected, scalp-compatible serum as the program's targeted care step. Use the product-directed frequency; do not assume all formulas should be applied daily.
Condition the hair fibers around the hairline during each wash. Use leave-in conditioning when needed to reduce friction and improve manageability.
Protect the hairline from repeated rubbing and document it consistently through the eight weeks.

guardrail: A hairline that is thinning, receding or developing smooth, shiny areas needs assessment by a dermatologist. Traction alopecia can become permanent if repeated tension continues.
guardrail_source: American Academy of Dermatology: Hairstyles that pull can lead to hair loss
kit: Improve slip and reduce friction during styling
Support your preferred low-tension style; it must not create tension or require aggressive brushing
weeks_intro: One wash day a week, small habits every day. Each week has one focus.
weeks: Audit bonnet, scarf, pillowcase and headwear friction.
Review edge brushing, styling gels and manipulation.
Compare comfort, breakage observations and styling habits with baseline.
Address any recurring tension or friction source.
Assess scalp comfort, irritation, dryness and consistency.
Change an irritating product if necessary.
Evaluate the routine and select the maintenance pathway.
wash_day: Allow cleanser to rinse through the lengths without scrubbing the edges.
Condition the hairline fibers and the rest of the hair.
Resume the serum according to its directions.
wash_day_note: Between wash days, maintain the low-tension styling and friction-protection habits.

Morning: Check for tenderness, itching, redness or irritation.
Apply the selected scalp serum according to its directions and your schedule.
Choose a comfortable style that does not pull at the temples or front hairline.
Avoid repeated edge brushing and tight slicked-back styling.
Evening: Check whether the hairstyle has become tight or uncomfortable.
Use a comfortable satin or silk bonnet, scarf or pillowcase.
Avoid tight elastic bands or headwear that rubs directly against the hairline.
Complete a second serum application only if the product's instructions call for it.

ingredients: Interesting early research on hair-follicle biology
Promising, not established topical regrowth treatment
Cosmetic support; not proven standalone regrowth
Used in some targeted scalp formulations
Helps condition hair fibers and improve feel
Improve slip and reduce combing friction
explainers: Green tea / EGCG: what the research shows

EGCG has been investigated in human hair-follicle organ culture and cultured dermal papilla cells. These findings are interesting, but they do not establish that a commercially available topical serum will regrow edges in people.

A 2025 systematic review of topical caffeine included nine clinical studies and 684 participants. Although results generally favored caffeine, three studies were rated medium quality, one low quality and five very low quality. The evidence is not strong enough to guarantee results from retail caffeine products.

expect: The program is designed to improve consistency of protective care and reduce avoidable tension and friction. Hair-fiber breakage may become easier to manage as the routine improves.
If the hairline is receding, thinning progressively or developing smooth, shiny patches, see a dermatologist rather than waiting for the program to finish.
